conventions.commits: Conventional Commits (e.g. `feat(core): add Swift language support with tree-sitter-swift handler (#1742)`); every commit GPG-signed with `git commit -S --signoff` and a `Signed-off-by:` DCO line (CONTRIBUTING.md lines 25-80).
conventions.testing: Unit tests live in-module under `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` in each languages/*.rs file (queries_compile, element match, inheritance happy and no-clause, defuse write site); registry tests in languages/mod.rs (lines 338-412) and lang.rs (lines 104-160); integration tests in crates/aptu-coder-core/tests/integration_tests.rs (TempDir plus analyze_file) and crates/aptu-coder/tests/ using common::call_tool_raw.
conventions.linting: cargo fmt --check; cargo clippy --locked --profile ci -- -D warnings -W clippy::cognitive_complexity; workspace lints deny unwrap_used, expect_used, undocumented_unsafe_blocks; unreachable_pub warn; SPDX header check and REUSE; cargo deny check advisories licenses bans plus the package-age script.
conventions.error_handling: Handlers are infallible and return Option<String> or Vec<String> (no Result); node text via bounds-checked get_node_text (languages/mod.rs); query compile failures become ParserError::QueryError and the language is reported as UnsupportedLanguage (parser.rs:228-300).

patterns: Language registry: one LanguageInfo arm per language in languages/mod.rs get_language_info, plus one arm in get_ts_language, plus a pub mod line.
Extension resolution: EXTENSION_MAP tuples in lang.rs drive language_for_extension, supported_extensions and the schema pattern.
Inheritance: java.rs and python.rs use child_by_field_name; swift.rs and kotlin.rs walk children by kind because the grammar has no fields (PHP follows the Swift/Kotlin style).
Capture contract: element queries wrap declarations in @function or @class and name them @func_name/@method_name or @class_name/@type_name (parser_elements.rs:285-300).
Def-use contract: captures prefixed write., writeread., read. classify sites; read captures at the same byte offset as a write are de-duplicated (parser_elements.rs:850-900).
Query files are Rust &str constants with an r"..." raw string, a leading newline and no trailing newline issue (java.rs, swift.rs, kotlin.rs).
Per-language handler modules start with the SPDX header and a //! doc line (swift.rs, css.rs; java.rs omits the doc line).

constraints: Maintainers implement this issue in-house; external PRs are closed (issue Note on Process), so the output is a plan, not a submission.

Language support is unconditional: the lang-* Cargo feature gates were removed (lang.rs header), so no feature flag is needed; languages/mod.rs and lib.rs doc comments still say feature-gated (stale).
Use tree_sitter_php::LANGUAGE_PHP, not LANGUAGE_PHP_ONLY, because the acceptance criteria require mixed HTML and PHP files to parse with zero ERROR nodes.
New Cargo.lock entries must be at least 7 days old (AGENTS.md; .github/scripts/check-package-age.sh); SKIP_PACKAGE_AGE_CHECK is not allowed for this issue.

tree-sitter-php 0.25.2 depends on tree-sitter-language ^0.1 (locked at 0.1.9) and has dev-dependency tree-sitter 0.27; the workspace pins tree-sitter 0.27.1 (locked 0.27.2), so no core upgrade is needed.
ELEMENT_QUERY and CALL_QUERY are mandatory: a compile error in either makes get_language_info-based parsing fail for php as UnsupportedLanguage (parser.rs:228-300).
Workspace lints deny unwrap_used and expect_used in non-test code and undocumented_unsafe_blocks; CI clippy adds -W clippy::cognitive_complexity.
Out of scope per the issue: .phtml/.inc/.module/.php5 extensions, trait use resolution, property and constant extraction, attributes, namespace aliasing, tool handler or schema changes.
Documentation drift to resolve or note: Swift is wired but absent from README Supported Languages and from lib.rs/mod.rs language lists; README and ARCHITECTURE.md count 18 languages.
test_coverage: Each existing language module has in-file unit tests: java.rs (element, inheritance, defuse write site, receiver handlers), swift.rs (queries_compile, set_language_smoke, element match, inheritance with and without clauses), css.rs (element, import, empty file). languages/mod.rs has test_get_language_info_known/unknown, test_get_ts_language_known/unknown, and a table test covering tsx, fortran, markdown, css, yaml (no php row yet). lang.rs has extension happy-path and edge-case tests and a schema-pattern test that iterates every EXTENSION_MAP entry (automatically covers php once added). parser.rs has compile-count tests (around line 1057 checks supported_languages().len()). crates/aptu-coder-core/tests/integration_tests.rs has per-language analyze_file tests (e.g. test_integration_tsx_analyze_file at line 3139). No existing test covers PHP, mixed HTML templates, or inheritance for interface/enum/trait.

library_findings.notes: Manifest read from tag v0.25.2 via gh api. php/src/node-types.json at v0.25.2 is identical to the default branch (302 entries). Node kinds used are confirmed there: class_declaration (fields name, body, attributes), interface_declaration (name, body; base_clause child), trait_declaration (name, body), enum_declaration (name, body; class_interface_clause and primitive_type children), method_declaration (name, parameters, body), function_definition (name, parameters, body), base_clause and class_interface_clause (children name|qualified_name|relative_name, no field), assignment_expression (left, right), augmented_assignment_expression (left, operator, right), update_expression (argument, operator), variable_name (child name), static_variable_declaration (name, value), simple_parameter (name, type, default_value), function_call_expression (function, arguments), member_call_expression and nullsafe_member_call_expression (object, name, arguments), scoped_call_expression (scope, name, arguments), namespace_use_declaration (type, body; namespace_use_clause children), named_type (child name|qualified_name|relative_name). Upstream tags.scm (queries/tags.scm) uses the same shapes for definition.class/interface/function and reference.call.

approaches.name: A: Full five-query handler plus extract_inheritance (recommended)
approaches.description: New languages/php.rs with ELEMENT_QUERY (function_definition, method_declaration, class/interface/trait/enum declarations), CALL_QUERY (function_call_expression, member/nullsafe/scoped call name fields), REFERENCE_QUERY (named_type), IMPORT_QUERY (namespace_use_declaration), DEFUSE_QUERY (variable_name writes and reads), and extract_inheritance walking base_clause and class_interface_clause children. extract_function_name, find_method_for_receiver and find_receiver_type are set to None, matching the issue's Not-in-Scope list. Wire php in mod.rs (pub mod, get_language_info with LANGUAGE_PHP, get_ts_language, test row), lang.rs (EXTENSION_MAP, supported_languages), Cargo (root, core, lock), README, plus unit tests in php.rs and one integration test file.
pros: Exactly matches the issue's Scope and acceptance criteria
DEFUSE_QUERY keeps PHP def-use compilable and covered by language tests (parser.rs:79-80 note)
Uses LANGUAGE_PHP, so mixed HTML/PHP templates parse with a text node and no ERROR nodes
Schema pattern and extension lookup update automatically from EXTENSION_MAP (schema_helpers.rs supported_file_ext_pattern)
cons: DEFUSE_QUERY has no production caller today (parser.rs:547), so its runtime value is test coverage only
PHP has no local_variable_declaration, so Java's DEFUSE_QUERY cannot be copied verbatim; write sites are assignment_expression with variable_name
Inheritance cannot use child_by_field_name: base_clause and class_interface_clause are unnamed children (Java-style walk returns nothing)

Crate age gate: v0.25.2 GitHub tag is dated 2026-11-19, about 9 days before 2026-11-28, so it likely clears the 7-day crates.io check, but crates.io publish date is unverified; v0.25.1 (tag dated 2026-10-06) is the safe fallback

approaches.name: B: Minimal extraction without DEFUSE_QUERY
approaches.description: Same as A but DEFUSE_QUERY omitted (defuse_query: None in the LanguageInfo arm), and php.rs exports only ELEMENT_QUERY, CALL_QUERY, REFERENCE_QUERY, IMPORT_QUERY and extract_inheritance.
pros: Smallest diff; no variable_name write/read heuristics to validate
Fortran and markdown already set defuse_query to None, so the pattern is accepted in-tree
cons: Fails the issue's Scope, which requires the five query constants including DEFUSE_QUERY, and the acceptance item for php.rs
PHP def-use sites are silently empty (parser_elements.rs:850 returns vec![] when defuse is None)
Leaves a visible gap against the Java, Swift, Kotlin and Python handlers

approaches.name: C: Java-parity receiver handlers
approaches.description: Approach A plus extract_function_name, find_method_for_receiver and find_receiver_type implemented on function_definition and method_declaration (walking up to class_declaration, interface_declaration, trait_declaration or enum_declaration), mirroring java.rs lines 1-80 handlers.
pros: Full parity with java.rs and kotlin.rs receiver tooling
Future-proofs receiver resolution if a consumer returns
cons: Explicitly Not in Scope in the issue; find_* handlers have had no consumer since #1807
Adds untested-by-production code paths and roughly doubles unit tests for handlers nothing calls
Reviewers would likely ask for it to be split out

recommendation: Approach A. It is the only option that meets the issue's stated five-query scope and acceptance criteria while avoiding the Not-in-Scope receiver handlers (C) and the silent def-use gap (B). Implement it as: LANGUAGE_PHP (not PHP_ONLY); no Java-style field walk for inheritance (iterate base_clause and class_interface_clause by kind); DEFUSE_QUERY written against variable_name instead of Java's local_variable_declaration; and pin tree-sitter-php to 0.25.2 only if the crates.io publish date clears the 7-day gate (check the crates.io page, which is not reachable from this environment), otherwise 0.25.1.

element_query_draft:
(function_definition
  name: (name) @func_name) @function
(method_declaration
  name: (name) @method_name) @function
(class_declaration
  name: (name) @class_name) @class
(interface_declaration

(trait_declaration

(enum_declaration

inheritance_walk_citation: Source: tree-sitter-php v0.25.2 tag, common/define-grammar.js (identical on default branch). (1) class_declaration (lines 365-373): optional(field('attributes', $.attribute_list)); repeat($._modifier); keyword('class'); field('name', reserved('classes', $.name)); optional($.base_clause); optional($.class_interface_clause); field('body', $.declaration_list). The base_clause and class_interface_clause nodes are UNNAMED CHILDREN, not fields: php/src/node-types.json lists only attributes, body and name as class_declaration fields, so child_by_field_name('superclass') or ('interfaces') (the Java walk) returns None. (2) base_clause (lines 334-337): keyword('extends') followed by commaSep1($._name). (3) class_interface_clause (lines 381-384): keyword('implements') followed by commaSep1($._name). (4) _name (lines 296-302): choice(alias(keyword('static')) -> name, cast-type names -> name, reserved('classes', $.name), $.qualified_name, $.relative_name). Walk: iterate node.child(i) for i in 0..node.child_count(); if child.kind() == 'base_clause', for each named child whose kind is name, qualified_name or relative_name push 'extends {text}'; if child.kind() == 'class_interface_clause', for each named child of kind name, qualified_name or relative_name push 'implements {text}'. The keyword tokens extends/implements are anonymous and never emitted. For 'class Foo extends Bar implements A, B {}' the tree is (class_declaration name: (name) (base_clause (name)) (class_interface_clause (name) (name)) body: (declaration_list)), giving ['extends Bar', 'implements A', 'implements B']. With no clauses the loop pushes nothing and returns []. Caveat: enum_declaration also carries a class_interface_clause (implements) plus a primitive_type backing type that must be skipped; interface_declaration uses base_clause for multiple extends. Qualified names keep their leading backslash in text (e.g. '\\App\\Base').

java_element_query_verbatim:
pub const ELEMENT_QUERY: &str = r"
(method_declaration
  name: (identifier) @method_name) @function
(class_declaration
  name: (identifier) @class_name) @class
(interface_declaration
  name: (identifier) @interface_name) @class
(enum_declaration
  name: (identifier) @enum_name) @class
";
java_defuse_query_verbatim:
pub const DEFUSE_QUERY: &str = r"
(local_variable_declaration declarator: (variable_declarator name: (identifier) @write.local))
(assignment_expression left: (identifier) @write.assign)
(update_expression (identifier) @writeread.update)
(identifier) @read.usage
";
defuse_required_rationale: DEFUSE_QUERY is typed Option<&str> in LanguageInfo (languages/mod.rs) and fortran/markdown pass None, so it is not compiler-enforced. It is required by (a) the issue Scope, which lists five query constants (ELEMENT_QUERY, CALL_QUERY, REFERENCE_QUERY, IMPORT_QUERY, DEFUSE_QUERY) and acceptance criteria for the php.rs file; (b) parser.rs build_compiled_queries compiles it into CompiledQueries.defuse, and parser_elements.rs:850 (extract_def_use) returns an empty vec when it is None, so PHP would silently get no def-use sites; (c) every sibling OO handler (java.rs:32, swift.rs:32, kotlin.rs:34) supplies one. Caveat: parser.rs:79-80 and parser.rs:547 state there is no production caller since the symbol tool removal; the query is kept for language-test coverage, so its runtime value today is test coverage only.
css_wiring_note: The "css" integration touches exactly: root Cargo.toml [workspace.dependencies] (line 49), crates/aptu-coder-core/Cargo.toml [dependencies] (line 54), lang.rs EXTENSION_MAP (line 45), languages/mod.rs pub mod (line 12), get_language_info arm (line 264), get_ts_language arm (line 330), and the table test row (line 389). It does NOT touch lang.rs supported_languages() (CSS is absent from it), so PHP adds that entry per the issue, not per the CSS precedent.
